citeAs: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar (2021). DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images. arXiv:2007.00398.
creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar (CVIT, IIIT Hyderabad; Computer Vision Center, UAB)
description: DocVQA is a large-scale dataset for Visual Question Answering on document images, consisting of 50,000 questions defined on 12,767 document images sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library. The dataset covers a variety of document types (forms, tables, letters, reports, etc.) and requires models to read and interpret text within the layout and structure of documents to answer natural language questions.
name: DocVQA
rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 2 independent annotations per question (stage 1 and stage 2 workers each provide answers); multiple ground truth answers per question were encouraged where warranted.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Answer mismatches between stage 1 and stage 2 annotators were flagged and sent for author review in stage 3. Questions flagged as inapt due to language issues or ambiguity were excluded from the dataset.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom web-based annotation tool (with Amazon support for the annotation effort)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation was organized in three stages. Stage 1: workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs, instructed to ask questions answerable from text in the image and enter answers verbatim. Stage 2: a different worker answered the same questions (without seeing stage-1 answers) and assigned one or more question types; questions could be flagged as inapt. Stage 3: if no stage-1 answer matched any stage-2 answer, the question was sent for author review, where questions and answers could be edited or accepted/rejected.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset prioritizes non-binarized images and pages with tables, forms, lists and figures, which may over-represent certain document types. Many documents are from food and nutrition related collections due to availability of non-binarized images. Most documents are from the 1960–2000 period. A large majority of questions start with "what is the", asking for date, title, total, amount or name.
rai:dataCollection: Document images were sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library, downloaded from different collections and hand-picked pages. Questions and answers were collected using remote workers via a web-based annotation tool in a three-stage process. The final set of images is drawn from pages of 6,071 industry documents spanning from as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Document images from the UCSF Industry Documents Library, spanning 5 industries (tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, chemical), covering documents from 1900 to 2018, including typewritten, printed, handwritten and born-digital text across many document types (letters, forms, reports, memos, tables, etc.).
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Documents span from as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018; most documents are from the 1960–2000 period.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataLimitations: Majority of documents in the library are binarized and binarization has taken a toll on image quality; binarized images were minimized but not eliminated. OCR errors can result in wrong answers even when models correctly ground questions. Models need to improve specifically on questions where understanding the structure of the document is crucial, and on figures, photographs, and handwriting.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Binarized images were minimized in the dataset to avoid poor image quality being a bottleneck. Pages with tables, forms, lists and figures were prioritized over pages with only running text. Questions flagged as inapt due to language issues or ambiguity were excluded from the dataset.
rai:dataSocialImpact: DocVQA aims to inspire a purpose-driven approach in document image analysis and recognition research, enabling intelligent reading systems that can respond to ad-hoc information requests from document images, with potential applications in document understanding and information extraction.
rai:dataUseCases: Visual Question Answering on document images; benchmarking document understanding models; driving purpose-driven document image analysis and recognition research; evaluating models that combine visual and textual cues for document comprehension.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: A commercial OCR application was used to extract OCR tokens from document images for use in baselines and upper bound computations.

evidence.name: We present a new dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images called DocVQA.
evidence.description: We present a new dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images called DocVQA. The dataset consists of 50,000 questions deﬁned on 12,000+ document images.
evidence.url: The dataset, code and leaderboard are available at docvqa.org

evidence.inLanguage: Workers were instructed to ask questions which can be answered using text present in the image and to enter the answer verbatim from the document.
evidence.citeAs: DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images Minesh Mathew1Dimosthenis Karatzas2C.V . Jawahar1
evidence.isLiveDataset: The DocVQA comprises 50;000 questions framed on 12;767images. The data is split randomly in an 80 10 10 ratio to train, validation and test splits.
evidence.rai:dataCollection: Images in the dataset are sourced from documents in UCSF Industry Documents Library. The documents are organized under different industries and further under different collections. We downloaded documents from different collections and hand picked pages from these documents for use in the dataset.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The ﬁnal set of images in the dataset are drawn from pages of 6;071industry documents. We made use of documents from as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018. Most of the documents are from the 1960-2000 period and they include typewritten, printed, handwritten and born-digital text. There are documents from all 5 major industries for which the library hosts documents — tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel and chemical.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: We made use of documents from as early as 1900 to as recent as 2018. Most of the documents are from the 1960-2000 period and they include typewritten, printed, handwritten and born-digital text.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionType: We downloaded documents from different collections and hand picked pages from these documents for use in the dataset. Questions and answers on the selected document images are collected with the help of remote workers, using a Web based annotation tool.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The annotation process was organized in three stages. In stage 1, workers were shown a document image and asked to deﬁne at most 10 question-answer pairs on it. The second annotation stage aims to verify the data collected in the ﬁrst stage. Here a worker was shown an image and questions deﬁned on it in the ﬁrst stage (but not the answers from the ﬁrst stage), and was required to enter answers for the questions. If none of the answers entered in the ﬁrst stage match exactly with any of the answers from the second stage, the particular question is sent for review in a third stage.
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Questions and answers on the selected document images are collected with the help of remote workers, using a Web based annotation tool. We thank Amazon for supporting the annotation effort
evidence.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: If none of the answers entered in the ﬁrst stage match exactly with any of the answers from the second stage, the particular question is sent for review in a third stage. Here questions and answers are editable and the reviewer either accepts the question-answer (after editing if necessary) or ignores it.
evidence.rai:annotationsPerItem: We encouraged the workers to add more than one ground truth answer per question in cases where it is warranted. The second annotation stage aims to verify the data collected in the ﬁrst stage. Here a worker was shown an image and questions deﬁned on it in the ﬁrst stage (but not the answers from the ﬁrst stage), and was required to enter answers for the questions.
evidence.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We tried to minimize binarized images in DocVQA since we did not want poor image quality to be a bottleneck for VQA. We also prioritized pages with tables, forms, lists and ﬁgures over pages which only have running text.
evidence.rai:dataUseCases: We introduce DocVQA, a large scale dataset of 12;767 document images of varied types and content, over which we have deﬁned 50;000questions and answers. We introduce a new data set and an associated VQA task with the aim to inspire a "purpose-driven" approach in document image analysis and recognition research.
evidence.rai:machineAnnotationTools: In all our experiments including heuristics and trained baselines, OCR tokens we use are extracted using a commercial OCR application.
evidence.rai:dataBiases: We use many documents from food and nutrition related collections, as they have a good number of non-binarized images. It can be seen that a large majority of questions start with "what is the", asking for date, title, total, amount or name.
evidence.rai:dataLimitations: Majority of documents in the library are binarized and the binarization has taken on a toll on the image quality. The models need to improve speciﬁcally on questions where understanding structure of the document is crucial.
evidence.rai:dataSocialImpact: We introduce a new data set and an associated VQA task with the aim to inspire a "purpose-driven" approach in document image analysis and recognition research. Our baselines and initial results motivate simultaneous use of visual and textual cues for answering questions asked on document images.
